data.title: Dollar jumps against yen as BOJ dissent clouds rate-hike outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • Yen drops after BOJ votes 7-2 to hike by 25 bps
  • Traders doubt BOJ commitment to further increases
  • Dollar ticks up, oil prices cool on easing supply fears

By Saqib Iqbal Ahmed and Harry Robertson

The dollar jumped against the yen on Friday after two policymakers at the Bank of Japan dissented from a widely expected decision to raise interest rates, raising doubt among traders about the likelihood of further hikes.

The BOJ pushed rates to their highest level in 31 years at 1.25%, yet the move did not boost the Japanese currency as traders felt there was a lack of explicitly hawkish guidance.

The decision, coming on the heels of the Fed's hawkish message from earlier this week, clears the way for further dollar strength, strategists said.

"(The) lack of hiking punch makes it easier for USD to go higher," Steven Englander, head of G10 FX research at Standard Chartered, said.

"The USD strength that we have been forecasting for the medium to long term may finally be here," Englander said.

The US dollar rose 1.2% against the Japanese currency to a two-week high of 157.897 yen after wavering during BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda's press conference.

It was set for its biggest daily increase versus the yen since December and the largest weekly rally since September 2024.

"They've just clearly underwhelmed versus expectations here," said Ray Attrill, head of FX strategy at National Australia Bank in Sydney.

"And I think that one of the more staggering aspects of it was that they couldn't even get the unanimous vote for that," he said. "That really raised eyebrows in the market."

Traders remained alert to the risk of intervention to prop up the currency after Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said Tokyo won't hesitate to conduct further coordinated action, following a joint US-Japan move to boost the yen in late July.

The yen rallied sharply in early September to its highest since February as traders bet the BOJ would embark on multiple rate hikes, although those wagers came under question on Friday.

ENERGY PRICES IN FOCUS

The rally against the yen helped the US dollar index climb 0.25% to 100.48, as broader currency markets remained focused on energy prices and the US Federal Reserve.

The index, which tracks the currency against six major peers, was up 1.4% for the week to around a six-week high after the US Federal Reserve hiked interest rates on Wednesday and signalled more increases could be coming.

Traders see a roughly 55% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Fed's next two-day meeting next month, up from 27% a week ago, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.

Oil prices slipped to their lowest levels in around a week on signs of easing supply pressures in Saudi Arabia.

China has asked Tehran to help rein in the Iran-aligned Houthis after their military blitz on Saudi Arabia over the past week, three Iranian sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The euro fell 0.1% to $1.14595 and was set to end the week 1% lower after the Fed's rate hike.

The British pound was also 0.1% lower at $1.335, giving up earlier gains after retail sales data beat expectations on Friday. The Bank of England held interest rates on Thursday but also suggested it could raise borrowing costs.

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin rose 4% to above $80,000 on Friday — its third straight day of gains — as it extended a rebound from Tuesday's sharp selloff, when the US Senate failed to advance comprehensive cryptocurrency legislation in a setback for digital-asset companies.

data.title: NAVER D2SF Invests in AI-Driven Precision Medicine Company ImpriMed
data.description:
• ImpriMed combines ex vivo functional testing with multimodal AI to support personalized cancer treatment decisions and drug development
  • The investment is part of ImpriMed's $10 million Series A2 bridge round as the company advances U.S. commercialization and expands into Asia
  • NAVER D2SF to strengthen its global healthcare founder community through its healthcare network and go-to-market expertise

SEOUL, South Korea, Sept. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NAVER D2SF, NAVER's inhouse corporate venture arm, has invested in ImpriMed, a Silicon Valley-based precision medicine company, joining ImpriMed's $10 million Series A2 bridge round. ImpriMed develops AI-driven precision medicine solutions that combine ex vivo analysis of patient-derived live cancer cells with genomic, immunophenotypic, and clinical data to support personalized treatment decisions. NAVER D2SF's investment reflects ImpriMed's commercial and clinical experience in the U.S. healthcare market and its growing capabilities across precision medicine and drug development.

Precision oncology increasingly relies on integrating multiple types of patient data to account for differences in disease biology and treatment response. ImpriMed applies multimodal AI to patient-specific cancer cell characteristics, drug response profiles, and clinical information to enable more personalized treatment selection.

At the core of ImpriMed's xCellSense® platform is its ability to keep patient cancer cells viable ex vivo for extended periods, enabling evaluation of their biological characteristics and drug sensitivity. The platform combines these results with immunophenotypic, genomic, and clinical data to guide treatment decisions. ImpriMed is developing AI models trained on more than 3.5 million data points, combining real-world data with functional cell analysis to improve predictive accuracy.

ImpriMed is preparing to commercialize products for blood cancers and blood infection, targeting FDA clearance and CLIA certification by Q1 2027 for an initial U.S. launch. The company has also established business partnerships with major U.S. hospitals as it builds its human health presence in North America. In South Korea, ImpriMed has developed software for multiple myeloma prognosis and therapy-response predictions. The software has been designated an Innovative Medical Device by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) and is progressing through the approval and commercialization process. ImpriMed also collaborates with leading tertiary hospitals, including Catholic University Seoul St. Mary's Hospital, Seoul Asan Medical Center, and Gangneung Asan Hospital.

ImpriMed's human healthcare expansion is supported by its commercial experience in veterinary precision oncology and its growing CRO business in drug development. In veterinary medicine, ImpriMed has performed more than 27,000 tests for canine and feline lymphoma to guide treatment decisions. A retrospective study showed a threefold increase in survival time and a fourfold improvement in treatment response, and the findings have been published in a peer-reviewed scientific journal. ImpriMed's solutions are currently used by more than 600 veterinary hospitals across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, and South Korea.

ImpriMed was co-founded in Silicon Valley by CEO Sungwon Lim and CTO Jamin Koo, who studied together at KAIST and Stanford University. The company brings together expertise in biomedical research, AI modeling, clinical collaboration, and commercialization. Beyond North America, ImpriMed plans to expand into the European and Asian markets.

The $10 million bridge round follows ImpriMed's $23 million Series A in 2023. The round was led by LB Investment, with participation from new investors NAVER D2SF, Samsung Securities, and Alois Ventures, as well as follow-on investments from existing investors BonAngels and Han River Partners.

NAVER D2SF continues to invest in healthcare startups targeting the North American market. Through NAVER D2SF's founder network, portfolio companies such as Soundable Health, PranaQ, and NubiLab share local market knowledge and operating experience, fostering collaboration across R&D and go-to-market strategy.

About NAVER D2SF

NAVER D2SF is NAVER's in-house corporate venture arm, supporting startups through investment and collaboration. Founded in 1999, NAVER has been Korea's leading search engine for more than 20 years and operates across commerce, content, fintech, and cloud services. Guided by its technology vision of D2 (For Developers, By Developers), NAVER continues to develop new technologies and build global partnerships.

To learn more, visit https://d2sf.naver.com.

data.title: Jones Soda Brings Iconic Fallout™ Nuka-Cola Flavors Into Reality With Exclusive "Vault-dweller Variety" Pack Ahead Of Fallout Day 2026
data.description:
Limited-Edition Collection Brings Drinkable Fallout™ Nuka-Cola Quartz and Nuka-Cola Cranberry Into Reality for the First Time Alongside Fan-Favorite Nuka-Cola Quantum

SEATTLE, Sept. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Jones Soda Co. () (OTCQB: JSDA) today announced the upcoming launch of the Jones x Fallout "Vault-Dweller Variety" 12-Pack, a club-exclusive beverage and collectible offering created to celebrate Fallout Day on October 23, 2026. The collaboration brings some of the Fallout universe's most recognizable Nuka-Cola flavors from in-game lore into the hands of fans and collectors.

Expected to begin shipping in late September ahead of Fallout Day, the "Vault-Dweller Variety" pack represents Jones Soda and Bethesda Softworks' fourth Fallout-themed club release and the next evolution of a highly successful retail program built around transforming beloved, critically acclaimed Fallout canon into real-world experiences through authentic flavors, immersive packaging, and collectible fan engagement.

The pack will be available exclusively at participating club retail locations throughout the United States and Canada.

For Fallout fans, October 23 is more than a date on the calendar—it is a celebrated community tradition. This year, club members will have the opportunity to participate in that celebration through a limited-edition collection inspired by decades of Fallout lore. Designed to transform iconic in-game Nuka-Cola varieties into real-world experiences, the pack combines collectible presentation, fan-favorite flavors and immersive Fallout storytelling in a way that brings the Fallout universe closer to reality than ever before.

The 12-pack includes four glass bottles each of:

  • Nuka-Cola Quartz — Inspired by the rare crystal-clear Nuka-Cola variety recognized by Fallout fans, consumers can now experience a flavor that has existed in Fallout lore for years.
  • Nuka-Cola Cranberry — Acknowledging the celebrated Nuka-Cola variety known throughout the Fallout universe, Cranberry is being brought into reality for the first time as part of this exclusive club collection.
  • Nuka-Cola Quantum — The legendary blue-glowing Nuka-Cola that became one of Fallout's most iconic and sought-after beverages returns as the centerpiece of the assortment, continuing its journey from game-world favorite to real-world fan phenomenon.

The club-exclusive collection also includes a custom Quartz-themed bottle opener and collectible caps, all housed in a specially designed, collector bag created to deliver a display-worthy experience for Fallout enthusiasts, collectors and gift-givers.

"With this fourth Fallout release in club retail, we wanted to create something worthy of Fallout Day and worthy of the incredibly passionate fan community that celebrates it," said Scott Harvey, Chief Executive Officer of Jones Soda Co. "The 'Vault-Dweller Variety' pack is about more than beverages—it's about bringing pieces of Fallout lore into reality. For the first time, fans can taste Nuka-Cola Quartz and Nuka-Cola Cranberry, alongside the returning fan-favorite Nuka-Cola Quantum, in a collectible package designed exclusively for club members. This collection represents exactly what we love about these partnerships: taking something fans have imagined for years and creating a way for them to experience it in the real world."

The club-exclusive launch is designed to give members a unique way to engage with the Fallout universe through a product that blends craft soda, entertainment fandom, and collectible value. By bringing Nuka-Cola Quartz and Nuka-Cola Cranberry from Fallout canon into reality, Jones Soda continues to reinforce the club channel as an exclusive destination for fans seeking unique, limited-edition experiences.

The specially designed package was created to stand out in-club and reward the treasure-hunt shopping experience club members value. From the glass-bottle assortment and collectible bottle opener to the included caps and display-ready presentation, every element was designed to feel like a rare discovery from the Fallout universe.

The Jones x Fallout "Vault-Dweller Variety" 12-Pack is expected to begin shipping September 11, 2026, ahead of Fallout Day on October 23, 2026, and will be available exclusively at participating club retail locations throughout the United States and Canada.

About Jones Soda Co.

Jones Soda Co.® is a leading craft soda company known for bold flavors, distinctive packaging and consumer-driven brand engagement. The Company markets and distributes premium craft sodas under the Jones® Soda brand across North America through retail, e-commerce and strategic partnerships. Jones Soda is headquartered in Seattle, Washington.

About Bethesda Softworks

Bethesda Softworks LLC, part of the ZeniMax Media Inc. group of companies, is a worldwide publisher of interactive entertainment software. Titles published under the Bethesda label include The Elder Scrolls™, Fallout™, DOOM™, QUAKE™, Wolfenstein™, Dishonored™, The Evil Within™, Prey™, RAGE™, DEATHLOOP™, Ghostwire™: Tokyo, and Starfield™. data.title: Morgan Stanley sees managed competition ahead of Trump-Xi summit
data.description:
The U.S.-China relationship is likely to remain in a phase of "managed competition" as President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping prepare to meet next week, with Morgan Stanley expecting the summit to focus on extending the existing trade and rare-earth truce rather than delivering a broader reset.

The Sept. 24 Washington meeting is likely to build on commitments from the May summit, with fewer new deliverables outside traditional trade measures and an extension of the rare-earth truce, Morgan Stanley said.

Trade truce remains the focal point

Morgan Stanley said the summit would be a test of whether the existing trade truce can withstand targeted escalation and extend beyond its Nov. 10 expiry. The firm said the two sides remain mutually dependent in areas including rare earths and chip exports while gradually building more distinct technology ecosystems.

Three measures are due to expire on Nov. 10: the suspension of the BIS Affiliates Rule, China's pause on its second-wave rare-earth controls, and 178 U.S. Section 301 tariff exclusions. Morgan Stanley expects both sides to prioritize extending those measures, potentially with modifications.

On tariffs, the firm expects some targeted rollback while the broader tariff framework remains intact. U.S. and Chinese teams are negotiating a framework covering roughly $30B of nonsensitive trade on each side, which Morgan Stanley said would be economically modest relative to total bilateral trade but could provide tangible progress without touching strategically sensitive areas.

The Trump administration is likely to delay announcing new tariffs on China and other countries related to alleged excess manufacturing capacity until after the Trump-Xi summit, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The administration had previously planned to release a trade report ahead of the meeting recommending a 7.5% tariff on Chinese goods, according to the background provided.

The timing of the tariff announcement and the eventual rate remain uncertain. Morgan Stanley said potential Section 301 overcapacity tariffs could remain an “overhang” even beyond the summit.

AI rivalry follows a separate path

While trade negotiations remain focused on preserving the existing framework, Morgan Stanley said competition over artificial intelligence is increasingly developing on a separate track.

The firm expects the U.S. to seek cooperation with China on monitoring AI-directed cyberattacks and discussions around AI regulation while pursuing a "middle path" on restrictions that would leave below-frontier AI capabilities relatively intact while controlling frontier technologies. China, meanwhile, is seeking greater visibility into how Washington will regulate future frontier models, Morgan Stanley said.

Morgan Stanley said the broader technology rivalry is likely to continue even if the trade truce is extended, with both countries pursuing greater supply-chain independence in areas including critical minerals, semiconductors, and AI infrastructure.

Market impact considered limited

Morgan Stanley said expectations for the summit are low, which could limit the market reaction to an extension of the trade truce. The firm said macro weakness, regulatory concerns, and liquidity headwinds remain more important near-term constraints for Chinese equities.

The firm also said the broader relationship would continue to be defined by sector-specific competition within a framework of managed competition. Its assessment was that the Washington summit would represent an effort to reinforce that framework rather than resolve the core disputes over advanced technology and critical minerals.

Morgan Stanley said the two countries' efforts to reduce strategic supply-chain dependencies would continue even under managed competition, supporting themes around economic security, reindustrialization, and AI sovereignty.

data.title: Fed's Bowman says overhaul of bank stress test will make process more transparent
data.description:
Key points:
  • Fed to vote on final stress-test version in coming weeks, Bowman says
  • Revamp would disclose stress-test models, equations, variables and more scenario details, she says
  • Fed expects to finish Basel and systemic-bank capital rule changes by year-end, Bowman says

By Pete Schroeder

The Federal Reserve's top regulatory official said on Friday the US central bank will soon finalize an overhaul of its "stress test" of big banks to make the process more transparent and the results more predictable for lenders, handing the industry long-sought reforms to the exam process.

Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said at an event in London that the central bank will vote on a final version of the revamped exam in the "coming weeks," which she said would "finally close the book on an opaque and unnecessarily unpredictable framework."

Banks have complained for years that the Fed's stress tests, put in place following the 2008 financial crisis and used to set additional capital requirements for the nation's largest lenders, are subjective and onerous. The industry sued the Fed in 2024 to challenge the use of the tests, and the central bank under Bowman put forward a series of proposed changes in October.

On Friday, Bowman said the new version of the test will shed far more light on the models the Fed uses to probe banks for weaknesses, including various equations, variables, and other technical details the central bank long kept secret from the industry. The new process will also provide more details on the hypothetical economic scenarios created each year for the test, changes Bowman said will allow the public a greater understanding of the testing process.

The Fed also plans to adopt a new rule that would average the results of a bank's two most recent stress tests when assigning capital requirements known as the "stress capital buffer." Bowman said this approach will reduce volatility in the capital that banks must set aside each year.

Going forward, Bowman said the public will be able to comment on the testing models, and the Fed intends to use its stress testing process to help privately inform supervisors of potential bank weaknesses. She added that banks are already conducting multiple internal stress tests on their own, and examiners and banks should have "open dialogue" on any relevant findings.

"I believe there is tremendous value in comparing notes," she said.

The push to complete the stress testing overhaul will be a major step in Bowman's efforts to transform, and in many cases ease, capital requirements imposed on banks. She added in her remarks that she expects the Fed will wrap up work on a pair of major capital rules by the end of the year: the so-called Basel rules on risk-based capital and a revamp of the additional capital charge applied to globally systemic banks, which the Fed anticipates will lower the capital large banks are required to hold in reserve.

data.title: Insurers Are Investing in AI and Private Credit, Moody's Survey Finds — WSJ
data.description:
By Heather Gillers

Life insurers' private credit binge won't end anytime soon, according to a survey out Friday from Moody's Ratings.

More than 40% of U.S. insurers polled by the ratings firm at the end of last year said they plan to increase their exposure to private debt. By Moody's estimates, private credit already accounted for 35% of life insurers' investments and 8% of property and casualty insurers' investments at the end of last year.

The survey also asked insurers about artificial intelligence-related holdings. It found that life and property insurers rated by Moody's hold roughly $8 billion and $2 billion respectively in data center-related assets. And they hold a further roughly $26 billion and $1 billion respectively in related energy projects.

Moody's estimates that the overall U.S. insurance sector has as much as $20 billion of exposure to data centers.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Soybean basis mostly flat as futures dive, corn bids mixed
data.description:
Spot cash basis bids for soybeans delivered to U.S. Midwest elevators and crush plants were mostly steady on Friday while corn basis bids were unchanged at elevators and mixed at processing facilities, grain merchants said.

  • Farmer selling was slow on Friday as Chicago Board of Trade futures prices dropped.

  • Spot soybean bids in the western Midwest remain well supported by strong demand from some processors for deliveries over the next week. Some crushers were short of needed supplies after harvesting delays due to rain and forecasts for more storms next week, merchants said.

  • A soy processor in Lincoln, Nebraska, offered a 50-cent-per-bushel premium for beans delivered by next Tuesday versus beans delivered later in September. Bids for soybeans delivered to a Council Bluffs, Iowa, crusher by Saturday were at a 90-cent premium over bids for beans delivered through the end of the month. A Sioux City, Iowa, crush plant also offered a 90-cent premium for deliveries by Monday.

  • CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were down 17-3/4 cents at midmorning on Friday at $13.02 a bushel, while December corn (CZ26) was down 4-1/4 cents at $5.26-1/4 a bushel.

data.title: Discover the evolution of Bajaj Pulsar 150, blending nostalgia with modern performance
data.description:
The Pulsar was destined for martyrdom. Most firestarters are no different. Given its sheer impact upon landing and the shockwaves it created, that it was going to make way for larger aspirations was perhaps an obvious outcome. Bullish as Bajaj may have been, the Pulsar was always going to breed fans — hardcore fans — but never loyalists. This is no great travesty and I don’t think it caught anyone at Bajaj off-guard. The Pulsar unlocked the idea that living a dream was, indeed, attainable. That you were going to transition to larger or differently-flavoured dreams is plain logic.

Now, 25 years after its breakthrough moment that not only revived Bajaj but rewrote its future, the Pulsar wants to do it all over again. How very romantic, right? It’s also rather problematic, though. Quite unlike Bajaj, a brand that has thrived on writing its own rules, its approach to this Pulsar revival is a bit inauthentic. While that’s a more philosophical concern, the execution, too, is unconvincing.

To me, the Pulsar was distinctive for its visual muscle and an engine that wasn’t shy of stealing attention from its sculpted bodywork. Between its twin-pod analogue instrument cluster, round (and later wolf-eye) headlight, bulbous tank, scooped-out side panels, shiny exhaust and a minimalist rear, the Pulsar had so many things rooting for it to become a design icon. The fact that it had the performance to match made it incomparably more exciting. Although, why did Bajaj have to revive a design that means little to a brand-new audience? If it were meant to evoke nostalgia for Pulsar alumni, then was a 150 (or a 125, also launched alongside) the right place to begin?

TEEN SPIRIT

I hadn’t even left the Bajaj Auto precinct in Akurdi, astride the Pulsar 150, when my mind had wiped its questionnaire clean. By the time I was past the main gate, I was already and completely occupied with the motorcycle between my legs. ‘It’s definitely a Pulsar, male or otherwise!’ I could hear myself think.

You don’t even have to get through all of its available gears to be able to tell this is a very engaging Pulsar and also, somehow, the most well-mannered of its kind. It’s refined but not enough to cannibalise its own feel, and that’s a tough balance to strike. If you’ve ridden a TVS Apache RTR 160 4V, you’ll know what this is about. There’s something about its combination of agility and spiritedness that’s distinctively unique to it, but now it happens at a level of modernity that’s in keeping with the times.

Starting from scratch has been a wise decision on Bajaj’s part. The oversquare engine in the P150 hasn’t changed in displacement (149.5cc), but it’s brand new. Now oil-cooled, it makes 13.8 bhp and 1.4 kg-m, both credible numbers. The double-cradle frame the old engine was mounted in has now been replaced with a tubular diamond type frame which uses the engine as a stressed member. The twin-shock rear, too, has now (and finally) been replaced with a monoshock. The most important outcome of these changes is weight savings. The new P150 boasts a 141-kg kerb weight which makes it 9 kg lighter as compared to the old one.

Of course, Bajaj has had to give in to demand for a strong feature suite, as inconsequential as it may be to real-world usage. You can have a Pulsar in three variants, all mechanically identical save for the exclusion of a rear disc on the lowest variant. The base variant gets a 5-inch colour LCD with Bluetooth connectivity and turn-by-turn navigation.

On the mid-spec bike, you get a 5-inch TFT with the same tech as on the base. The top variant gets a split seat and the addition of Google Maps mirroring. Ride modes are common to all variants as is the 260-mm front disc. In effect, with prices ranging between Rs 1.15 lakh and Rs 1.23 lakh, and with a grand separating the mid (Rs 1.22 lakh) and top variants, your decision will be dictated by the last three digits of your EMI.

Okay, it’s fun and well-equipped, but what’s with the nostalgia? I tackle mine in three layers — form, function and feel. On form, to me, the Pulsar scores the lowest. The happily familiar front end can’t, for a moment, distract me from the Discover-ish (and weak) tail section. I’m not a fan of the visual muscle it’s lost by the way of adopting a monoshock, a slimmer exhaust and blacked-out cycle parts. A Pulsar may have become a commuter (a long time ago, actually), but it doesn’t have to look like one.

EASY DOES IT

If nostalgia is about function, we have a story. The Pulsar 150, armed with its readiness, makes easy work of craftily cutting through the city and, to my surprise, it had more to offer once we got onto the highway. Cruising at 90 kph, I had to dab the brakes for traffic until I was down to about 55 kph and I didn’t need a downshift to get back up to higher speeds again.

If I were younger (in other words, not as attuned to the flavour of larger motorcycles), I’d happily do a Mumbai-Pune commute on it, as I used to in my twenties. It’s fast enough and its responses are adequately exciting. Past its mid-range, there is a buzz (strongest at the right footpeg), but in the business of getting to places quickly and economically, that’s hardly a deterrent.

When the corners arrived, the Pulsar leaned in confidently. It feels almost too civil to be a Pulsar and yet, what it means to a new generation of riders can’t be ignored. If the Pulsar is to serve as a start point to your motorcycling life, you’re having it better than most before you have. Braking is strong and intuitive, too, although the single-channel ABS means you can lock up the rear rather easily; probably how a 20-year old would like it anyway, I suppose. Over bad roads, the front end feels pliant, although I found the rear to be set up on the firm side. Again, not something a younger and healthier person would struggle with, perhaps.

At the end of a 70-km stint, I wasn’t quite done with it. The new Pulsar 150 is a really likeable motorcycle, clearly the most competent of its kind, and I think its performance is as magnetic as its poise. It is, in fact, when you view nostalgia from the lens of ‘feel’ that the Pulsar appears to have exceeded its brief. It could have stopped at feeling engaging, which it comfortably is, but it also feels evolved. I like it not just for what it does, but for what it indicates could be the direction of all the larger Pulsars to follow. Funnily, though, I’d have said the same thing if I’d viewed all of it objectively, too. Can we just leave nostalgia alone, please?

@TheMotorGram

data.title: Maruti Suzuki Baleno: A new face with the same comfort
data.description:
If the Baleno’s facelift was meant to serve as a distraction from its switch to a three-cylinder engine, I’m not falling for it. A face has rarely decided the fate of a car in India (last-gen Creta, anyone?) and, in any case, Maruti Suzuki needn’t have bothered because its Z12E 1.2-litre engine is a gem. Keen enthusiasts will be able to tell it isn’t a four-cylinder engine, but it is in no way a dud. There’s more to this update than just an engine (or a face), of course. The Baleno now features ventilated seats for the front row and also ADAS, which makes it even more value for money than it already was.

All right, now, I’d call the Baleno’s front end polarising if it actually were. It isn’t, though. The overblown three-slat ‘grin’ looks completely disjointed from the rest of the car’s likeable (if unexciting) lines and to think it’s a canvas for more aftermarket chrome is dreadful, to put it politely. The rest of the Baleno is unchanged (thankfully?), with the exception of a shark-fin antenna, a small bit of trim on either side of the bonnet and some new colours.

The cabin is a two-tone affair (black and blue), a theme that applies to the dashboard, door trim and seats, and it’s very spacious. No changes here and none needed either. The front row of seating is fantastic even for long driving days and the addition of ventilation (three levels, activated through two buttons wedged between the charging ports) is just terrific news. At level three, the ventilation mechanism is too loud; I suppose it’s great for that initial burst on a hot day, but at levels two and one it’s usable and a definite value addition. It needs to be rebooted every time you restart the car, though.

Kitted out

There’s is also Level 2 ADAS and the controls aren’t screen-dependent, fortunately. You get a stack of switches on the dash (to the right of the steering wheel) that allows you turn off the lane-keep assist and emergency-braking functions; a three-second-long press deactivates these. In other news, there’s a decent Clarion sound package and a 9-inch infotainment screen with an intuitive user interface. Wireless Android Auto and Apple CarPlay are standard on all except the base (screenless) Sigma variant; the Delta variant gets a 7-inch touchscreen.

What you get as standard across all variants of the Baleno is comfort. This is a large hatchback with inherently excellent space management and, for a family of four or even five, it’s compelling enough to make you look past, say, a Dzire. I wish the rear seats offered better under-thigh support, though, and I did find myself sitting somewhat knees-up. In the same breath, I’ll add that it rides really well. Even over some of the roughest roads I could find, it held its own admirably, and highway stability, too, is impressive.

Effortless drive

Coming to the Baleno’s party piece, the 81.8-bhp Z12E engine is responsive and quick off the line and, except at near-idle speeds, you’ll struggle to tell if it has three cylinders and not four. Acceleration isn’t thrilling, perhaps, but there’s no real-world scenario in which it feels strained or inadequate. At city speeds, the drive experience is effortless, and on the highway, you can cruise at the speed limits comfortably. Road noise does creep into the cabin quite intrusively beyond 100 kph, though. While the AMT isn’t the sharpest tool in Baleno’s arsenal, it can’t be outdone on convenience. The CNG variants (₹7.92 lakh onwards) only get a manual gearbox, though.

Where the Baleno (facelift or otherwise) scores equally high is in its ease of driving. It’s easy to find a comfortable driving position and outward visibility is quite good. The steering feels light, the brakes feel confident and, in the city, it all comes together to give you an effortless drive.

With prices ranging between ₹5.99 lakh and ₹9.99 lakh (ex-showroom), the Baleno is as good as no-brainers can get. It’s practical, spacious and well-equipped, and its real-world performance is as appealing as its fuel efficiency. As for that face, you’ll just have to learn how to park nose-in, I suppose.

@TheMotorGram

data.title: India’s raw jute prices continue to rule high, but improved supply helps mills run full shifts
data.description:
Raw jute prices continue to rule high despite a higher crop size this year. But jute mills, which had suspended operations due to acute raw jute shortage, are relieved to be running full shifts again.

Jute mills faced a challenging period till July and August amid uncertainty over raw jute availability. Prices, which touched ₹19,000 a quintal in early July, have eased to around ₹12,500 a quintal with the new crop arriving. This is still around 50 per cent higher than the year-ago level of around ₹8,500 a quintal.

“Last year’s shortage created a gap in the supply pipeline. Once the pipeline gets replenished, the prices of raw jute should stabilise. There is no one who is having huge stocks right now. Farmers are releasing the material in a phased manner,” said Manish Poddar, Managing Director, Budge Budge Company, and Anglo India Jute and Textile Industries.

Bangladesh ban

“As there is no raw jute shortage now, mills are running full. Prices are not killing the mills. The shortage was killing the mills. There was no jute available last year,” Poddar told businessline.

An insufficient raw jute crop last year created a difficult situation for the jute industry throughout the season. Prices had started rising from the beginning of the jute year 2025–26 as crop size remained depressed at around 76 lakh bales of 180 kg each compared to around 75 lakh bales in 2024-25. Significantly, India’s raw jute production in 2023-24 was 90 lakh bales.

After Bangladesh abruptly announced a ban on the export of raw jute from September 2025, domestic raw jute prices had experienced an abnormal escalation. At least 14 jute mills across the Hooghly industrial belt in West Bengal had either suspended operations or were facing severe production disruptions due to non-availability of raw jute and unviable costs. Many mills operated at 10–15 shifts per week, far below sustainable levels. Worried about further price escalation of raw jute and uncertain availability, even relatively better-placed units were conserving the raw material.

Quotes suspended

Although the Jute Commissioner imposed raw jute stock limits on the industry to ensure equitable distribution within the industry and to prevent hoarding by mills and traders, by June this year raw jute prices were close to ₹20,000 a quintal — roughly three-and-a-half times the Minimum Support Price (MSP) — and the Jute Balers’ Association (JBA) suspended its daily quotation altogether for the month of June, an unprecedented step.

Raw jute prices started easing from August 15 with the new crop arriving in the market in bulk quantities. For the jute year 2026-27, crop size is estimated to be around 92-95 lakh bales as higher remunerative prices for farmers have pulled acreage back into jute. Satellite mapping by NRSC-ISRO has shown the area under the crop is up by 20 per cent to 5.82 lakh hectares from 4.80 lakh hectares in 2025-26.

According to industry participants, raw jute prices continue to rule high compared to the same time last year as new arrivals in the market have been less than 15 lakh bales so far, with farmers holding back part of their produce to book higher profits. Moreover, the continued ban on the export of raw jute by Bangladesh has contributed to the high prices.

Market healing itself

“The industry was anticipating that the arrivals of raw jute would be much more because the prices were so good. Obviously, farmers would book their profits at these levels, but it seems that they are still holding back. I would reasonably assume that when the prices are decent, the normal human tendency is to book profits because you are getting significantly above your cost of cultivation,” said Hemant Bangur, Chairman, Gloster Limited.

“Because the arrival has almost been equal to the consumption for the mills so far, there is almost no stocks in their go downs. I don’t think on average the stock in most of the mills today is more than 10 days of consumption. On the domestic front, high jute prices are not affecting us as much because whatever price we are paying to the farmers ultimately gets passed on to the government as a larger part of the good supply goes to the government,” Bangur pointed out.

For jute mills, government’s order book for foodgrain sacking is the most robust this year.

“Raw jute at about ₹12,500 is not a warning sign — it is the market healing itself: down from a scarcity peak of ₹19,000 in early July, still well above the ₹5,925 MSP, and finally rewarding the farmers who were forced to sell below MSP for two seasons,” said Sanjay Kajaria, former chairman, Indian Jute Mills Association (IJMA).

Exports unviable

“This is the level at which the whole chain works — the grower earns, mills can procure lawfully and honour FCI’s sacking orders, twenty reopened units are bringing workers back before Puja, and exports are secured; what would threaten industry is not a fair farm-gate price, but a slide back below MSP that pushes the farmer to maize cultivation,” Kajaria said.

On the overseas front, Indian exporters of jute goods suffered severely last fiscal as high increases in raw jute prices could not be absorbed by export customers, who were already affected by high freight scenario and tariff-related concerns in the global economy. As a result, exports became uneconomical, leading to a sharp decline in exports across the jute industry.

“Exports are really being affected because our raw jute prices are significantly higher than Bangladesh’s raw jute prices. So the price that we are able to quote in the international markets based on our cost is much higher than Bangladesh’s. On top of that, Bangladesh has introduced cash subsidies on jute exports, and their cost of production is also lower than ours. So that is impacting us in the export market,” Bangur said.

Land ports plea

Jute Products Development & Export Promotion Council (JPDEPC) Chairman Gopal Saraf said the council has urged the Centre to intervene in opening the land ports in West Bengal to allow importing of raw jute from Bangladesh.

“I hope that it will soon be resolved and prices of raw jute will come down. We are having many meetings with the ministry (Ministry of Textiles), and we are trying to make a five-year plan on how we can increase exports of jute goods,” Saraf told businessline.

The UK and European Union trade agreements are expected to help exporters improve market access this fiscal through lower or zero import duties, he added. Notably, the UK and US are the two major export markets for India’s jute products.

data.title: D2C brands, brokers flag concerns over proposed UPI MDR
data.description:
D2C brands and discount brokerage firms are raising concerns over the proposed merchant discount rate (MDR) on UPI payments, with businesses across sectors warning that the additional payment cost could put pressure on margins and, in some cases, force them to rethink how they absorb transaction costs.

For D2C companies, the concern comes at a critical time as brands enter the festive season, when sales volumes rise but so do expenses on discounts, customer acquisition, marketplace commissions and listing fees. Founders said even a 0.4 per cent MDR could become significant when applied to large transaction volumes.

“UPI has become an integral part of the D2C checkout experience because of its convenience and high consumer adoption. While a 0.4 per cent MDR may appear small at an individual transaction level, for growing D2C brands processing significant volumes, these costs add up and have a direct impact on contribution margins, especially during the festive season when discounting and customer acquisition costs are already elevated,” said Utkarsh Sahu, Co-founder & CEO, Hunnit.

Sahu said Hunnit would be reluctant to pass the cost on to consumers, given the potential impact on checkout conversion.

“At Hunnit, we would be reluctant to pass this cost on to consumers because friction at checkout can directly impact conversion. In the short term, brands will likely absorb the cost, but over time it will make payment costs another important line item that D2C businesses have to actively optimise,” he added.

Another founder of a personal care brand, speaking off the record, said brands are likely to absorb the cost initially, but the MDR would further squeeze already-thin margins. The founder said the timing was particularly challenging because festive sales come with additional costs such as marketplace commissions, listing fees, discounting and marketing.

The concerns are similar to those being raised by discount brokers including Groww, Zerodha and Angel One, which have sought changes to the proposed MDR framework. Brokers have argued that the ₹300 cap does not meaningfully address the economics of capital-market transactions and have sought a much lower effective charge, including a 2-basis-point MDR with a ₹2–5 cap.

They have also sought an increase in the MDR-free transaction threshold from ₹2,000 to ₹20,000, arguing that capital-market transactions have different ticket sizes and payment patterns.

UPI has so far operated largely on a zero-MDR model for merchants, with banks and other ecosystem participants supported through government incentives and other revenue streams. The proposed framework would introduce MDR on applicable transactions, making the level of the charge and exemption thresholds important for businesses that rely heavily on UPI for collections.

For D2C brands, founders said the issue is particularly sensitive because UPI has become a core part of the online checkout experience.

“A sustainable payments ecosystem is important. The ideal framework is one that allows banks and payment platforms to continue investing in UPI infrastructure without diluting the affordability and simplicity that made UPI so transformative for Indian consumers and digital-first brands,” Sahu said.

data.title: Cash-return stocks win back investor favor, leaving megacaps behind
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US indexes turn redDow is weakest off ~0.5%, Nasdaq strongest, off ~0.1%
  • Energy leads S&P 500 sector gainers; Materials is biggest loser
  • Euro STOXX 600 index down >1%
  • Dollar, gold rise; US crude up ~0.9%; bitcoin rallies >5%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~4.99%

CASH-RETURN STOCKS WIN BACK INVESTOR FAVOR, LEAVING MEGACAPS BEHIND

Companies that prioritize returning cash to shareholders through dividends and buybacks are back in favor with investors this year in a reversal from the past two years, according to a report from Morningstar.

The firm says that its Dividend and Buyback index, which is heavily weighted towards high-yielding sectors such as financial services, energy stocks and consumer defensive companies, gained over 31% from the start of the year through August.

That has comfortably outperformed Morningstar's US Total Market Index, which is up about 14% for the same period. The last time it beat the broad market was in 2022, Morningstar said.

Shares of companies using cash for dividends and buybacks are winning across sectors, said Dan Lefkovitz, an indexes strategist at Morningstar, including in technology, where legacy firms such as Cisco , Dell and Texas Instruments are having "monster years."

Cisco and Texas Instruments offer dividend yields of 1.56% and 2.18% respectively, while Dell offers 0.45%, according to LSEG data.

Technology firms have contributed to over 15% of the Dividend and Buyback index's growth so far this year, the report published on September 9 showed.

Dell has surged four-fold in 2026, making it the third-best-performing stock on the S&P 500, trailing only data storage firm Sandisk and Moderna , which have jumped seven-fold and five-fold, respectively.

The S&P High Yield Dividend index (.SPHYDA) has climbed about 9.6% so far this year, already on pace for its best performance since 2021. State Street's SPDR S&P Dividend ETF tracking this index has jumped 10%.

Among market-leading megacap companies, Nvidia , Apple and Microsoft , with their yearly gains between 2% and 23%, have underperformed the high-yielding stocks.

Tesla and Amazon.com have never paid a dividend, while Meta Platforms and Alphabet only began payouts in 2024, offering dividend yields of 0.31% and 0.26% respectively.

Their relatively low dividend yields, and buyback programs that have not kept pace with their soaring share prices, keep the group out of the Dividend and Buyback index altogether, Lefkovitz said.

data.title: Meta's personal AI agent Muse hits No. 1 on Apple's App Store
data.description:
Meta Platforms' Muse app, a personal AI agent that goes beyond a chatbot and executes multi-step tasks on a user's behalf, has reached the No. 1 spot on Apple's U.S. App Store a little over one week after its release.

The app quickly rose above its competitors, as OpenAI's ChatGPT sits at No. 2, Google Gemini is No. 8 and Anthropic's Claude comes in at No. 13. Way down the list, SpaceXAI's Grok lands at No. 32 and Microsoft Copilot ranks No. 64.

"Anyone can use it out of the box, no technical experience required," according to Meta. "It can handle tasks, like sending an email or booking travel, and it can take on big audacious goals. Once a person shares a goal with Muse, it helps them develop a personalized plan and coordinate their time and resources, then advances the work on its own. It can open a browser, fill out forms, and negotiate on their behalf."

Muse can also keep working in the background even when a user has closed the app and can check in for approval before completing certain tasks.

"A week after launch, Muse is now the #1 app in the App Store!" said Meta Chief AI Officer Alexander Wang in a post on X on Friday. "It's been SO exciting to see how much y'all have done with Muse. We can't wait to do more together!"

data.title: Prysmian, Rio Tinto partner to bring low-carbon aluminum to Amazon data center
data.description:
Italian cable maker Prysmian said on Friday it had partnered with Rio Tinto to supply electrical cables made with low-carbon aluminium for an Amazon data centre in Ohio.

The cables will use aluminium produced with ELYSIS "inert-anode" technology, which Prysmian said eliminates direct greenhouse gas emissions from the smelting process, releasing pure oxygen instead.

  • Project is the first known use of inert-anode-smelted aluminum in a data center, the company said.

  • "The use demonstrates that the carbon footprint of data centers can be reduced at the raw material level," it added.

  • Prysmian will manufacture the cables at its Sedalia, Missouri facility.

  • The project builds on the collaboration announced by Prysmian and Rio Tinto in March 2026.

  • Joern Tinnemeyer, Vice President of Data Center Engineering at Amazon Web Services (AWS), linked the initiative to the company's 2040 net zero target.

data.title: Maharatna PSU stock Power Grid to raise Rs.5,000 crore through bonds: Check issue size, tenure and details
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 18 -- Power Grid Corporation of India has approved a plan to raise up to Rs.5,000 crore through the private placement of bonds, giving the power transmission company another fundraising route. The decision was taken by the company's Committee of Directors for Bonds at a meeting held on September 18, 2026.

The proposed issue is for unsecured, non-convertible, non-cumulative, redeemable and taxable POWERGRID Bonds - LXXXIV (84th) Issue 2026-27. The company informed the stock exchanges that the fundraising will be carried out through private placement.

The total size of the proposed bond issue has been fixed at Rs.5,000 crore. This includes a base issue of Rs.1,000 crore and a green shoe option of Rs.4,000 crore.

The bonds are proposed to be listed on both the BSE and NSE. They will have a tenure of 10 years from the deemed date of allotment, with annual redemption payments beginning from the end of the fourth year.

The coupon or interest rate on the bonds has not yet been decided. Power Grid said the coupon, interest payment schedule and principal payment details will be finalised after bidding on the Electronic Book Provider (EBP) platform.

The bonds will be unsecured, meaning they will not have any specific charge or security created over the company's assets. The filing also stated that there are no special rights, interests or privileges attached to the instruments.

Power Grid also disclosed that there had been no delay of more than three months in the payment of interest or principal, and there were no comments or letters regarding non-payment of interest or principal on the due dates or any other matter related to the security or assets.

The company said details relating to redemption of preference shares and debentures were not applicable.

The PSU stock ended 2.5% higher at Rs.270. Despite the gain, the stock has remained under pressure in recent months, declining 0.5% in one month, 8% in three months, 11% in six months and 8% over the last one year. Over a five-year period, however, it has delivered multibagger returns, rising 101%. The stock hit a 52-week high of Rs.324.80 in April 2026 and a 52-week low of Rs.250 in February 2026.

On the financial front, Power Grid Corp. recorded a 0.9% year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit for Q1 FY27, which came in at Rs.3,598 crore, below the Street estimate of Rs.3,866.5 crore. Revenue from operations increased 2.7% YoY to Rs.11,497 crore, but also missed market expectations.

Despite the lower-than-expected profit and revenue, the company saw improvement at the operating level. Ebitda rose 4.3% YoY to Rs.9,536 crore, while the Ebitda margin widened to 82.9% from 81.7% in the year-ago period.

Power Grid Corporation of India is a state-owned power transmission company responsible for transmitting electricity across India.

It operates one of the country's largest power transmission networks and also has businesses in telecom and consultancy services related to the power sector.

data.title: StubHub Stock Rises After Citi Upgrade on 'Robust' Downloads — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Ty Roush

Shares of StubHub rose Friday after Citi analysts upgraded the stock on expectations that "robust" downloads will boost ticket sales, offering a potential lift after the World Cup failed to offset the platform's mounting costs.

StubHub stock added 4.3% to $6.20, distancing itself from its 52-week low of $5.88 reached Tuesday.

Citi analysts wrote Friday that they believe StubHub will report third-quarter adjusted Ebitda above expectations thanks to robust app downloads, allowing the ticket reseller to deliver full-year adjusted Ebitda "near the high end" of StubHub's guidance of $420 million.

"As such, we are upgrading StubHub to Buy," analysts said.

Third-quarter downloads are expected to have increased to 1.4 million, up from 1.2 million in the prior quarter, with projections for another 800,000 downloads through the fourth quarter, Citi analysts wrote.

Even with an expected resurgence in downloads, Citi lowered its price target for StubHub shares to $7 from $9, citing the potential impact of an MLB lockout.

Wall Street anticipated the FIFA World Cup to lift StubHub's business, with Morgan Stanley analysts writing in May that the event could "prove a meaningful tailwind for the secondary ticketing industry." That month, StubHub reported earnings that showed an increase in ticket demand.

But StubHub's spending outpaced the "record" quarterly revenue of $573.1 million that CEO Erik Baker reported in August. The ticket platform posted a second-quarter loss attributable to common stockholders of $40,000, while its expenses surged 37%.

StubHub's stock has dropped 75% through Thursday from its trading debut in 2025. Its initial public offering was priced at $23.50.

Recent weakness in StubHub shares is driven by fears that the company will miss adjusted Ebitda guidance and that AI could disrupt its business in the long run, Citi analysts said.

StubHub is expected to report third-quarter earnings in November.

data.title: Robust U.K. Retail Sales Could Play Into BOE's Inflation Fears — Market Talk
data.description: The rebound in British retail sales in August could raise inflationary worries for the Bank of England, RSM U.K. chief economist Thomas Pugh says in a note. Sales rose 0.5% on month in August despite rising oil prices. That is a good sign growth isn't going to fall off a cliff in the third quarter, he says. But the BOE Thursday warned if demand continues to hold up in the face of higher energy prices, it will make it easier for firms to pass on rising input costs to consumers. "Today's retail sales data will play into that fear," Pugh notes. That dynamic would push up inflation, making an interest-rate hike more likely later this year, he says. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)
